concerns.concern: Temperature independence of the suppression radius does not exclude Joule heating. With µW dissipated locally, the hot-spot size is set by power and barely depends on bath temperature. A quantitative thermal model, and ideally an on-chip resistive heater control, is needed to separate heating from non-equilibrium pair breaking.
concerns.quote: The statement "Joule heating can be excluded because the quenching does not depend on temperature" therefore needs a quantitative thermal model.

concerns.concern: The authors' own hot-spot model predicts temperature dependence, because the critical non-equilibrium density and the relaxation time should change strongly near T_c. Yet the fitted r₀(P) is identical at 0.4 K and 5.6 K. The film's T_c is not stated in the main text.
concerns.quote: Temperature independence is unexpected within the authors' own hot-spot model.

concerns.concern: The experiments run at µW powers and hundreds of nA leakage, about 1000 times the powers of transport GCS. The leakage shows signs of oxide degradation, so the imaged effect may be a breakdown-adjacent regime rather than the same phenomenon.
concerns.quote: The imaged phenomenon may therefore be a high-dissipation, breakdown-adjacent regime. It may not be the same effect that switches nanowire supercurrents.

concerns.concern: No transport GCS data (critical current vs gate voltage) are shown on the same films or chips. The headline claim that GCS is a genuine feature of superconductivity beyond transport is therefore unsupported, and the title and abstract framing should be adjusted.
concerns.quote: the main text shows no transport GCS data (critical-current suppression vs V_G) on the same films or chips.

concerns.concern: The Pearl length (~2.9 µm) is comparable to the device size and to r₀. The field edge is therefore smeared, and the quoted ~0.1 µm uncertainties in r₀ are unjustified without simulated inverse-problem tests and a comparison of both extraction methods on the same dataset.
concerns.quote: the field step's position responds only weakly to the boundary position. The quoted r₀ uncertainties (~0.1 µm, Fig. 3a) need justification

concerns.concern: The model assumes a sharp, fully normal disk, but the order parameter should vary continuously. The measured r₀ may only mark partial suppression, so the abstract's claim of complete suppression is not demonstrated. A graded superfluid-density model should be tested.
concerns.quote: The abstract's claim of "complete suppression … exceeding 1 µm" is not demonstrated by the data.

concerns.concern: Gate-polarity independence rules out vacuum field emission, but it is equally expected for any dissipation-driven mechanism, including Joule heating. It therefore does not discriminate between heating and non-equilibrium particles.
concerns.quote: It therefore does not discriminate NEPs from heating.

concerns.concern: Within each temperature dataset, r₀ correlates strongly with |V_G|. The collapse onto power instead of voltage relies on run-to-run drift of the onset voltage. Comparing matched power at deliberately different V_G (e.g., different gap widths or leakage resistances) is needed.
concerns.quote: The collapse onto P rather than V_G relies on the drift of V_G^ON between runs.

concerns.concern: Excluding a direct electric-field effect is trivial here, since such a field is screened within ångströms and could never produce µm-scale suppression. The exclusion says little about nanoconstrictions.
concerns.quote: Excluding it here therefore says little about nanoconstrictions.

concerns.concern: The two-parameter Lambert-W hot-spot fit discriminates little, since almost any saturating mechanism would fit comparably well. Alternatives (thermal, 2D in-film diffusion, ballistic phonons) are not compared, and no goodness-of-fit or parameter correlations are reported.
concerns.quote: Almost any saturating mechanism would fit Fig. 3a comparably well.

concerns.concern: The 3D isotropic infinite-medium Green's function is inconsistent with the layered SiO₂/Si stack, where phonons travel ballistically in silicon at sub-K. Interpreting r_d (comparable to the oxide thickness) as a single-medium diffusion length is questionable.
concerns.quote: The interpretation of r_d as a diffusion length in a single medium is therefore questionable.

concerns.concern: The abstract claims a quasiparticle lifetime of ~10⁻⁹ s, although the text admits the diffusion origin cannot be determined. The estimates rely on room-temperature glass diffusivity and on a diffusion constant from NbN-type nanowires.
concerns.quote: The abstract states a quasiparticle lifetime of ~10⁻⁹ s. The main text concedes that it "is not possible to determine"

concerns.concern: In-film quasiparticle diffusion is hard to reconcile with the quenching observed when the island is floating and the source sits ~0.8 µm away from it.
concerns.quote: In-film quasiparticle diffusion is also hard to reconcile with the observation of quenching when the island is floating

concerns.concern: The location of the dissipation source and the actual leakage path (across the gap, along the surface, or into the substrate) have not been independently verified. Post-measurement microscopy for filaments or damage sites is suggested.
concerns.quote: The source location and the actual leakage path have not been independently verified.

concerns.concern: Parasitic wiring leakage (~60 GΩ) contributes to the measured leakage current, so the power actually dissipated at the device is uncertain at low power. It should be subtracted, and constant-power mode should be used for all datasets.
concerns.quote: The power actually dissipated at the device is therefore uncertain at low P.

concerns.concern: The penetration depth changes substantially between 0.4 K and 5.6 K. The effect of this on the Bx-step extraction method, which is referenced to the zero-gate map, is not discussed.
concerns.quote: How this affects the Bx-step method referenced to the V_G = 0 map is not discussed.

concerns.concern: Film inhomogeneity, vortices and non-superconducting grains may bias r₀, especially at low power. Vortices invalidate the first extraction method for part of the data, and their impact on the second method is not shown.
concerns.quote: Inhomogeneous films and pinned flux may bias r₀, especially at low P.

concerns.concern: The reduced quenching in the displaced-source (G4–G5) and extended-gate configurations is only called consistent with the model. No quantitative prediction from the fitted parameters is compared with the data.
concerns.quote: A quantitative prediction from the fitted r_d and P_d is not compared with the data.

concerns.concern: Only two temperatures were measured. A series with several points approaching T_c, together with reported T_c, λ(T) and Pearl length, would be far more diagnostic.
concerns.quote: A temperature series with several points approaching T_c would be far more diagnostic than two temperatures.

concerns.concern: The vortex–GCS interaction lacks a systematic dataset (escape power vs temperature, field and gate distance). Its non-monotonic temperature dependence is anecdotal; the reviewer asks for such a dataset or a move to the Supplement.
concerns.quote: Without it, the non-monotonic temperature dependence (0.45 K, 3.5 K, 5.8 K) remains anecdotal; otherwise move it to the Supplement.

concerns.concern: The dimensionality of Eq. (1) (3D Green's function) and the units of the density ρ should be clarified.
concerns.quote: clarify Eq. (1) dimensionality (3D Green's function) and the units of ρ

concerns.concern: Reference [13] has a year/DOI mismatch.
concerns.quote: correct the year/DOI mismatch in ref. [13]

concerns.concern: The phrase stating that measurements span from well below the gap to above the critical temperature of Nb is confusing, given the temperature-independence argument.
concerns.quote: the closing statement that the measurements span "to above the critical temperature of Nb" is confusing in this context.
